subject: Bar chart with differing bar widths.

messages.author: 2448dffd44f05372
messages.subject: Bar chart with differing bar widths.
parts:
Good day all,

Discovered ggplot2 last week and I'm since a big fan, albeit one
that's only on Chapter 5 of the book.. This is my first post, so
apologies for any errors. I'll base it on a 'template' I've seen after
searching the mailing list.

==Goal:
I'm trying to plot a horizontal bar chart, whose bar widths differ in
size.

==Minimal Sample Data/Code:
myData<-data.frame(Group=LETTERS[1:9],
Size=seq(100,4000,length.out=9),Growth=seq(30,-20,length.out=9))
myP<-ggplot(myData,aes(Group,Growth,size=Size))
# Draw a horizontal bar chart
myP+geom_bar()+coord_flip()

==Output
The bars' widths are all the same. I realise this may not be the
appropriate geom to use and tried:

myP+geom_line()

but that didn't show anything on the layer and instead shows a legend
with Sizes..

Any help on this would be much appreciated.

Regards,

Jorge.



--

messages.subject: Re: Bar chart with differing bar widths.
parts:
The solution turns out to be elementary (I guess that's why no one
bothered to reply...). Basically, one needs to plot one bar at a time
and specify its width. It's done manually below but a loop with a
properly scaled bar width variable would do.

Sample code:

myP<-ggplot(myData,aes(Group,Growth))
myP+geom_bar(aes(Group,Growth),data=myData[1,],width=0.01*myData[1,"Size"])
last_plot()+geom_bar(aes(Group,Growth),data=myData[2,],width=0.01*myData[2,"Size"])
etc.

Hope this helps whoever needs to do this one day.

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: Bar chart with differing bar widths.
parts:
I looked at it earlier and couldn't get anything to work. That's why
I didn't reply. I was waiting for someone more knowledgeable.

Your solution is not very elegant; but don't take that as being
harsh. You at least got something that worked which is better than
what I got.

I played with it some more and finally got an error message that made
sense and got me on the track to something that worked.

ggplot(myData, aes(Group, Growth, width=0.001*Size)) +
geom_bar(stat="identity", position="identity") +
coord_flip()

I bumped the width down two orders of magnitude so it would be more
reasonable. Width can be an aesthetic, controlled by the data, so it
can be in the original aes(). What you were missing is that with pre-
summarized data, you need a stat="identity" argument to geom_bar.
Otherwise, it tries to summarize (bin) the data for you. Also,
apparently, "position_stack requires constant width", so I added a
position="identity" argument as well. Since there is only one set of
data, there is no difference in the positions.

Hadley, why is width not documented in geom_bar? (help page or
http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_bar.html ) Is it experimental and
interactions like this have not been worked out, or is that an
oversight?

--Brian Diggs

parts:
Hi Brian,

thank you for taking the time to respond. Clearly my presumption
earlier that elementary questions are not answered was wrong and will,
in the future, be more patient and won't be afraid to post no matter
how trivial.

- You have highlighted something important below re the 'width'
argument -- I basically discovered it by luck when looking at some
other person's post.
- Also, I think the data would have to be transformed first to add a
scaled 'width' variable (say 0.1 to 1) that maps the data one wishes
to plot with the width of the bars. I found that linear interpolation
between the data points i.e minimum value = 0.1, max value = 1,
produces better results than a random scaling factor.

Thanks once again,

Jorge.
